findings.summary: GET handler imports drizzle-orm and db/schema and queries notificationRules through app.container.db directly; the route also maps rows to DTOs.
findings.fix: Move the query to notifications/repository (listRules), expose it via NotificationService, route only calls the service.

findings.summary: Service constructs an Octokit client itself with process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN instead of using the GitHubClient port.
findings.fix: Use `await this.container.github()` and `createIssueComment` from the GitHubClient port; the token comes from SecretsProvider.

findings.summary: POST handler validates the body with NotificationRuleInput.parse(req.body) instead of declaring it in the route schema.
findings.fix: Add `body: NotificationRuleInput` to the route `schema` so invalid input is rejected 422 before the handler.

findings.summary: The domain core imports drizzle-orm, db/client and db/schema, creates a DB handle (line 32) and queries history itself.
findings.fix: Compute dismiss stats in a server repository and pass them into a pure calibrateFindings(findings, stats, config).

findings.summary: The domain core imports @anthropic-ai/sdk and builds a client from process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead of receiving an LLMProvider.
findings.fix: Accept an injected LLMProvider (contracts/ports.ts) as a parameter and call llm.complete().

findings.summary: The domain core reads calibration.config.json from disk (readFileSync + process.cwd()).
findings.fix: Pass CalibrationConfig in as an argument; load and validate it in the server.

findings.summary: Service takes FastifyRequest/FastifyReply, resolves context from the request and sets status codes and headers.
findings.fix: Service takes plain arguments (workspaceId, repoId, window); routes.ts owns getContext, status codes and headers.

findings.summary: buildAndSaveDigest runs the whole use case in the data-access layer: aggregation, the health classification (line 75) and an LLM call via container.llm (line 77).
findings.fix: Repository keeps only queries/insert; orchestration and the LLM call move to DigestService, the health rule to a pure helper.

findings.summary: Imports listRunsForPull from another module's internals (../reviews/repository/run.repo.js).
findings.fix: Go through the reviews module's public API (its repository facade/service) or a shared query in db/rows, not a deep import.

findings.summary: DigestRepository is constructed with the whole Container rather than a Db handle, which is what lets the LLM call leak in.

Weekly digests are scheduled with an in-process setInterval started from route registration (digests/routes.ts:16): lost on restart, runs once per API instance, failures swallowed by .catch(() => {}).
findings.fix: Register a `digests.weekly` job kind on container.jobs and trigger it from the platform scheduler/poller; the handler calls DigestService.

findings.summary: The reviews module imports and instantiates NotificationService to react to a finished review, fire-and-forget with errors swallowed — a direct module-to-module dependency that will become a cycle.
findings.fix: reviews enqueues a `review.completed` job (container.jobs.enqueue); notifications registers the handler for it. Neither module imports the other.

findings.summary: A failed GitHub comment is retried with an in-memory setTimeout that re-runs the whole notifyForReview: lost on restart, re-posts comments for rules that already succeeded, errors swallowed.
findings.fix: Post each comment as a job (container.jobs.enqueue) and rely on JobRunner's persisted retries/backoff; the service does not schedule its own retries.

findings.summary: scheduler.ts queries t.repos through container.db outside a repository.
findings.fix: Add a repository method (e.g. listReposForDigest) and call it.

findings.summary: The reviews barrel re-exports its data access with `export * from './repository/run.repo.js'`, publishing every query function (and anything added later) as the module's public API.
findings.fix: Export only the public API (services/types); drop the repository re-export and the blanket `export *`.

findings.summary: notifications imports the reviews query function listRunsForPull through `../reviews/index.js` and calls it with its own Db — reaching into another module's data layer via the barrel.
findings.fix: Get run totals through a reviews service method (or a deliberate shared query in db/rows), not the reviews repository.

findings.summary: digests imports from the repo-intel module (STALE_INDEX_AFTER_MS, RepoIndexStatus via ../repo-intel/index.js). digests → repo-intel is not an allowed cross-module edge.
findings.fix: Either get the index status through a port/service the platform exposes, move the shared constant/type to @devdigest/shared, or add a reviewed digests → repo-intel row to the allow-list in the same PR.

findings.summary: notifications imports DEFAULT_MIN_SEVERITY from the settings module (../settings/index.js). notifications → settings is not an allowed cross-module edge.
findings.fix: Move the default to @devdigest/shared or the notifications module's own constants, or add a reviewed notifications → settings row to the allow-list.

severity_scale.note: Labels are matched case-insensitively. If the review defines its own legend (e.g. 'blocker / must-fix / nit'), its tier order wins over this list. An unlabeled finding takes the level of its section (e.g. 'Блокує мердж' → blocker). Severity floor is met when the given level ≥ min_severity (blocker > should-fix > nit).

false_positive_levels.scope: Only statements that assert one of a file's `forbidden_claims` (same meaning, any wording or language) are false positives. Anything in that file's `allowed` list, and any other opinion about the file that does not assert a forbidden claim, is not counted. One statement covering two files counts once per file whose forbidden claim it asserts.
false_positive_levels.blocking: A forbidden claim given at blocker or should-fix level (or unlabeled inside a blocking/should-fix section).
false_positive_levels.nit: A forbidden claim given at nit level or hedged as a suggestion ('краще було б через job').
false_positive_levels.not_counted: Allowed opinions, context mentions, explicit 'this is fine', correctness notes.
